g.text: Second Renaissance: a theory of change people can argue with
Co-initiate a Second Renaissance: a conscious transformation of foundational views, values, practices, and
institutions toward a wiser, weller, regenerative civilization.
Hold the stewarded review: invite the people the trees affect, circulate the model first, agree what 'good…
Hold the stewarded review: invite the people the trees affect, circulate the model first, agree
what 'good enough for provisional use' means, and keep minority reports
Owner: The 2R research circle (steward to be named)
Carries out, from the Transition Tree: Facilitate one bounded stewarded review of the goal,
What we expect to see: A dated model records confirmed, disputed and still-provisional items,
the evidence for each, a named steward, a decision rule and the next review date
Stop if: The review runs past its time box, or disagreement is being smoothed over to reach
The first prerequisite since June is still open: decide together how the trees change. Who
will steward a time-boxed review of the goal, the main problems and the constraint
Every later step (a throughput definition, an entry path, recurring practice) assumes trees
the group has accepted. The count shows no change to the trees from late July through
August, and nothing merges into them yet: the first prerequisite from June, deciding
together how the trees change, is still open.
· as of 28 September 2026 · 24 steps to get here ·
This is the Second Renaissance's shared reasoning: a movement's strategy written as trees, then argued with,
reorganised and partly rebuilt by the people working on it. Step back through how it got here, or look at the one
